CBS News: Senate report details Secret Service failures in response to Trump assassination attempt in Butler
NBC News: Would-be Trump killer practiced 100-yard shot day before Pennsylvania assassination attempt, FBI documents show
Fox News: Thomas Crooks shifted from pro-Trump to anti-Trump online before shooting, report says
ABC News: Senate report highlights resources denied for Trump events in 2024
PBS News, Associated Press: Questions remain at Secret Service one year after Trump rally shooting
CNN: James Copenhaver, wounded in 2024 Trump assassination attempt, dies at 76

WLT Report: Todd Blanche says FBI found new Butler information after Trump claims Wray-era files were altered

content.p: On the evening of Saturday 13 July 2024, former President Donald Trump was a few minutes into a campaign speech at the Butler Farm Show grounds in Pennsylvania when a 20-year-old man opened fire from the roof of a building outside the rally. One bullet grazed Trump's ear. A firefighter in the crowd, Corey Comperatore, was killed, and two other spectators were critically wounded. A Secret Service counter-sniper shot the gunman, Thomas Crooks, dead at the scene.

Because Crooks died there, there was never a trial. What is known about the attack comes from federal investigators, congressional committees and an inspector general, and their findings are mostly about the Secret Service's failures, not about the gunman. More than two years later, the FBI has still not established why he did it.

Thousands of people came to the roughly 100-acre fairground in the afternoon heat. CBS News noted that the county had backed Trump by a wide margin in 2020, so a friendly crowd was expected. Trump stepped up to the podium at 6:02 p.m., CBS News reported, and its video timeline puts the first shot at about 6:11 p.m. NBC News reported that Crooks fired eight shots with an AR-15-style rifle.

Video analysed by CBS News showed bystanders pointing at the roof and shouting in the minutes before the first shot, at least two minutes before it, the network said. Butler County Sheriff Michael Slupe described a local officer who tried to reach the roof, only to let go and fall back when the gunman turned toward him. CBS reported that the first shot came while Trump was speaking about immigration. Secret Service agents surrounded Trump, who had blood running down his face, and took about a minute and a half to get him off the stage. He raised his fist several times and appeared to say "Fight", CBS reported. He wrote on Truth Social that a bullet had "pierced the upper part of my right ear".

Comperatore, 50, a firefighter and father, was shot in the head and killed. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said at a news conference the next day that Comperatore's wife had asked him to tell the public that her husband "died a hero" and that he had dived on his family to protect them.

David Dutch, 57, and James Copenhaver, 74, were critically wounded. Copenhaver, from Moon Township, told a local television station that a bullet had torn into his triceps and another remained in his body, leaving him with nerve damage and the need for a cane. He and his wife, Marianne, sued the federal government in June 2026, alleging negligence by the Secret Service. Copenhaver died on 23 September 2026, aged 76. His family said he died surrounded by loved ones. The county medical examiner did not disclose the cause, and one of his lawyers declined to say whether his injuries had contributed, citing the pending lawsuit.

The FBI has released 600 pages of newly unclassified files, with interviews of Crooks's relatives, neighbours, teachers and classmates. NBC News reported that they describe a young man who became increasingly absorbed in guns and long-range shooting. He had practised at a local sportsmen's club the day before the rally, according to a person who remembered him there. Crooks's father said he had developed the interest during the Covid pandemic. He worked about five years as a dietary aide at a nursing and rehabilitation centre and was due to study engineering at Robert Morris University, having earned an associate degree at the Community College of Allegheny County.

Classmates told investigators that he was occasionally bullied but that the bullying was never considered excessive. He was a registered Republican who was critical of both parties, and he gave $15 to a Democratic-aligned group in 2021, according to the files as NBC reported them. NBC noted that it had not independently verified the documents the New York Post cited in its reporting on Crooks's father. Federal records obtained by Fox News, and summarised by the WLT Report, show he took delivery of gun parts under the alias "Bob Dole" and that an anonymous donor paid for his cremation.
content.h2: Motive, as the FBI states it
content.p: The FBI has not named a motive. Patel wrote on X that the investigation, run by more than 480 FBI employees, found that Crooks had limited online and in-person interactions, planned and carried out the attack alone, and did not share his intent with anyone. Agents conducted more than 1,000 interviews, examined more than 2,000 public tips, seized 13 devices, reviewed half a million digital files and found 25 of his accounts on social media and forums, Patel said. Authorities told Congress that his laptop showed no particular ideology, Fox News reported. Fox also cited the New York Post's report, drawn from digital records and an unnamed source, that his online comments shifted over several years from pro-Trump to anti-Trump. Senator Chuck Grassley said in September 2026: "We don't know anything about the motivation [of] why [Crooks] wanted to kill Trump."

The Senate Homeland Security committee's interim report, released on 25 September 2024, listed planning, communications and security failures that it said "directly contributed" to the attack, including no clear chain of command, poor coordination with state and local police, inadequate resources and failure to secure the site. The chairman, Gary Peters, said every one of the failures was preventable. The report found that Secret Service personnel were notified of a suspicious person carrying a rangefinder 27 minutes before the shooting, but that the lead agent and other site officials told the panel they never received the information. CBS reported in 2024, citing sources, that the notification came about 20 minutes before. The radio systems on site also had chronic problems, according to the report.

The committee's final report, from Chairman Rand Paul on the first anniversary, mostly confirmed the earlier findings. It said Secret Service headquarters had denied multiple requests for staff, assets and resources during the campaign, including at least two for Butler. Paul said former director Kim Cheatle made false statements to Congress in saying that no requests for Butler had been denied; she responded that she had directed additional assets to the rally. The Associated Press reported that the Secret Service's own inquiry found that supervisors had expected farm equipment to be placed to block a line of sight, and that it was not. The agency said six staff members were suspended without pay for 10 to 42 days. Cheatle resigned; the Senate report said the penalties were too weak.

The Department of Homeland Security's inspector general published its own report on 30 June 2026. Its team interviewed 92 people, received more than 70,000 documents and built a 3D model of the site. It concluded that the Secret Service had "missed multiple opportunities to detect, prevent, and disrupt" the attack. Failures it listed included an under-trained operator and malfunction that left a drone flight undetected, no joint communications room with local police, and intelligence about a long-distance threat that was not shared with the Pittsburgh field office's leadership or the lead and site agents. The Secret Service agreed with all seven recommendations, and the inspector general considered three of them closed.

President Joe Biden said that "there's no place in America for this kind of violence". In September 2026 Trump alleged, without releasing documents, that the Butler attack was a Democratic plot and that investigation records were missing, altered or corrupted when he returned to office, and he said that former FBI Director Christopher Wray should "pay a price". Attorney General Todd Blanche said at a White House briefing that the FBI had found new information about Crooks's background and history and sent it to the Senate, but he did not identify it or offer evidence for a plot. Patel told senators that investigators had found no evidence that Crooks communicated with anyone other than his parents, according to the WLT Report. The Associated Press added that a separate incident in September 2024, in which an armed man was spotted outside one of Trump's golf courses and shot at by an agent, also raised questions about the agency's performance.
